summary: Malati J. Shendge is an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, Akira Hirakawa, and R. D. Vadekar.

Malcolm David Eckel studied at the University of Oxford and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, he held administrative posts at Harvard and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Boston University (1990–2024).
Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar who studied at Ravenshaw Girls' High School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami, a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki. He taught at Kyoto University as assistant (1965), associate professor (1975), and professor (1984, 1993, 1996–2001), and later at Otani University.
Indologist Manabendu Banerjee served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society and was attested as Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University in 2003.

Indologist and philosopher Mandan Mishra held posts at the University of Rajasthan, served as principal of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), and was Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1993–1996).

Manfred B. Steger studied under Robert Baker Aitken, at the University of Hawaiʻi, and at Rutgers University. Working in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at Illinois State, RMIT University (2005–2011), and the University of Hawaiʻi (2011–2016).

Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein, and served as full professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube studied at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller from 1949 to 1953. Specializing in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig in 1991.

Mangal Deva Shastri, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1919–1922) under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1937–1946).

Manik Man Bajracharya specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the Lotus Research Centre, Documenta Nepalica, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018), and the University of Heidelberg (attested 2023).

Manlio Iofrida studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore (~1969–1973). Working in philosophy, he held posts at the University of Pisa (~1984–1992) and the University of Bologna (~1992).

Manshi Kiyozawa, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa. He held posts at Toyo University and became the first dean and founding president of Otani University (~1901–1902).
Manu Leumann was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).
Manudeva was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa and Bālaśarman Pāyaguṇḍe.

Marc Aurel Stein was an archaeologist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and held posts with the University of the Punjab and the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and was also taught by Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.
Linguist Marcel Cohen studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi between ~1905 and 1911. He later held posts at the University of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954).

Marcel Granet studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. A scholar of sinology and religious studies, he held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.
